extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using SMPL.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by combining 15 existing motion capture datasets. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet, while others were obtained privately or recorded by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Missing markers due to occlusion are handled by updating the pose prior weight as a factor of the number of missing markers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets with varying markersets ranging in size from 37 to 91 markers.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: When hand markers are missing, hand poses are imputed by setting them to the average pose of the MANO model.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Mocap data is converted into realistic 3D human meshes represented by a rigged body model (SMPL) using a method called MoSh++.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual inspection was performed to correct or hold out problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be continuously expanded with more mocap data contributed by the authors and the community.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Identity-dependent shape parameters and 3D body scans of subjects.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current runtime for the MoSh++ method used to generate the dataset is not real-time.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We combine 15 existing motion capture datasets into one large dataset: the Archive of Mocap as Surface Shapes (AMASS)... The publicly available datasets were downloaded from the intemet. We obtained several other datasets privately or recorded them ourselves (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM).

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The publicly available datasets were downloaded from the intemet. We obtained several other datasets privately or recorded them ourselves (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM).

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses... To address this, we introduce a coefficient... This updates the pose prior weight as a factor of the number of missing markers.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: AMASS, a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets... The source datasets all contain varying markersets ranging in size from 37 to 91 markers

rai:dataImputationProtocol.evidence: In cases where there are no markers present on the hands of the recorded subjects, the hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We achieve this using a new method, MoSh++, that converts mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by a rigged body model; here we use SMPL

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, we manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We achieve this using a new method, MoSh++, that converts mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by a rigged body model

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by us and the community.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: The vertex positions of SMPL are adapted according to identity-dependent shape parameters

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The consistent representation of AMASS makes it readily useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep leaming.
